headline: Newly unredacted court papers in Kentucky's lawsuit against Character.AI give specific examples of chatbot conversations the state says pushed users toward self-harm and extreme dieting.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: the unredacted filing was on 7 Oct 2026 and our 9 Oct edition carried it; this article adds examples, not a new development.
importance_line: Children, teenagers and vulnerable users and their families are affected first, then regulators and chatbot companies facing similar state suits, but the chats are allegations in a court filing, the ages of all users are not given and the company's reply is missing.
summary: WLKY reports that Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman filed an unredacted version of the state's January lawsuit against Character Technologies, maker of the Character.AI chatbot platform, giving examples of alleged chats in which bots insulted a user's appearance, suggested starving to lose a quarter of body weight and advised a user considering self-harm (our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried the filing; the examples and Coleman's phrase 'ill-planned, uncontrolled experiment' are new here). The state asks the court to require stronger safeguards for young users and to hold the company financially accountable; these are the state's allegations, the filing does not give every user's age, and the article carries no response from the company.
notes: Follow-up of the item carried in our 9 Oct 2026 edition (item 80, Reuters via UA.News and CNA). The unredacted complaint was filed 'Wednesday' (7 Oct 2026). WLKY says the state calls this the first case in the nation against an AI chatbot company; the summary does not repeat that claim as fact. Article contains references to self-harm; the summary keeps the examples non-graphic.
